question.title: Design a URL Shortener
question.subtitle: Design a scalable service that converts long URLs into short links and redirects users to their original destinations.
learningObjectives: Estimate request rates and storage requirements.
Design APIs for URL creation and redirection.
Select a suitable persistent data store.
Evaluate basic availability and failure scenarios.

problemStatement.short: Design a service that converts long URLs into short URLs and redirects visitors to the original destinations.
problemStatement.full: Design a URL-shortening service similar to Bitly. Users should be able to submit a long URL and receive a short URL. When another user visits the short URL, the system should redirect them to the original destination. The service should support high redirect traffic, generate unique short codes, and remain reliable as traffic grows. Design the high-level architecture, APIs, data model, and request flows. Explain your key decisions and identify potential bottlenecks.
learnerTask: Design the high-level architecture using the component canvas.
Define how URLs are created and resolved.
Choose suitable storage and caching strategies.
Review the evaluation report and improve the design.

functional.title: Create a short URL

The system generates or allocates a short code.

functional.title: Redirect to the original URL
functional.description: A request containing a valid short code redirects to the corresponding original URL.
acceptanceCriteria: The redirect request reaches a resolver.
The resolver can retrieve the URL mapping.
The system returns an HTTP redirect to the client.
The design provides a valid lookup path through its selected storage strategy.

functional.title: Maintain short-code uniqueness
functional.description: Two different URL mappings must not unintentionally share the same short code.
acceptanceCriteria: The design includes a uniqueness strategy.
Concurrent creation requests are considered.
A collision does not silently overwrite an unrelated mapping.

functional.title: Handle unknown short codes
functional.description: The service returns an appropriate not-found response when a short code does not exist.
acceptanceCriteria: The resolver handles missing mappings.
The client receives a defined error response.
A missing mapping does not produce an invalid redirect.

functional.title: Support high-volume redirects
functional.description: The design supports a substantially higher redirect rate than URL creation rate.
acceptanceCriteria: The redirect path can be scaled horizontally or through another justified capacity strategy.
The design accounts for read traffic.
The learner identifies potential storage or application bottlenecks.

functional.title: Validate submitted destinations
functional.description: The service validates URLs before storing them.
acceptanceCriteria: The system validates URL syntax and permitted schemes.
The system does not blindly redirect to malformed input.
Security risks associated with open redirects and abuse are considered.

hints.text: Which operation do you expect to happen more frequently: creating a short URL or redirecting a visitor?
Think about the creation path and redirect path separately. They perform different operations and may have different traffic patterns.
The redirect path repeatedly looks up mappings by short code. Which storage access pattern would make that lookup efficient?
If many requests resolve the same popular short codes, consider whether a cache could reduce repeated database reads.
A possible redirect flow is: client request, application resolver, cache lookup, database lookup on cache miss, and redirect response. Consider what happens when the cache is unavailable.

rules.title: Valid component references

rules.passCondition: All node types are supported and every edge references existing nodes.

rules.title: Compatible connection semantics
rules.check: Every connection type is compatible with the source and target operations.
rules.passCondition: All connections conform to their declared semantic contracts.

rules.title: URL creation path exists

rules.passCondition: All required capabilities are present and connected in a valid creation flow.

rules.title: Redirect resolution path exists
rules.check: Verify that a redirect request can reach a mapping lookup and produce a redirect response.
rules.passCondition: A valid lookup and response path exists.

rules.title: Short-code uniqueness
rules.check: Verify that the design addresses identifier collision and concurrent creation.
rules.passCondition: The architecture provides a supported uniqueness strategy, such as an atomic unique constraint or equivalent allocation mechanism.

rules.title: Unknown-code handling
rules.check: Verify that missing mappings produce a defined not-found response.
rules.passCondition: The design includes missing-record handling and error response behavior.

rules.title: Redirect capacity strategy
rules.check: Evaluate the redirect path against the required traffic and configured capacities.
rules.passCondition: The supported model indicates that required components can handle the configured workload.

rules.title: Destination URL validation
rules.check: Verify that URL validation and permitted-scheme controls are represented in the request path.
rules.passCondition: The design identifies an appropriate validation control.

rules.title: Redirect latency estimate

rules.passCondition: The estimated latency is below the target under the declared model assumptions.

rules.title: Redirect throughput
rules.check: Compare the target request rate with the modeled capacity of components on the redirect path.
rules.passCondition: No modeled required component exceeds its configured capacity.

rules.title: Mapping integrity
rules.check: Verify that the chosen data store or allocation process can enforce unique short-code mappings.
rules.passCondition: The design includes a valid uniqueness mechanism.

rules.title: Application redundancy
rules.check: Assess whether application instance failure leaves a viable request path.
rules.passCondition: At least one healthy application instance and a viable routing path remain in the modeled failure scenario.

rules.title: Durable mapping storage
rules.check: Verify that successful URL creation persists mappings in a component marked as durable.

flows.name: Create URL
steps: Application generates or allocates a short code.
Application persists the mapping with uniqueness enforcement.

strengths: Provides a clear durable source of truth.
limitations: The database may become a read bottleneck.
Application capacity must be evaluated against the workload.
A single database instance may be a reliability limitation.

referenceSolutions.name: Cached redirect architecture

flows.name: Create URL
steps: Application generates or allocates a short code.
Application writes the mapping to the durable database.

flows.name: Redirect
steps: Load balancer routes the request to an application instance.
On a cache hit, the application obtains the destination from the cache.
On a cache miss, the application reads the database and may populate the cache.

strengths: Provides a useful architecture for studying read-heavy workloads.
limitations: Cache misses still reach the database.
Cache availability and eviction affect performance.
Cache stampedes and hot keys may require additional handling.
A cache does not replace durable storage.
tradeoffs: Lower expected database load versus added operational complexity.
Cache freshness versus expiration and invalidation complexity.

referenceSolutions.name: Key-value storage architecture
strengths: Aligns storage access with lookup by short code.
Can support horizontal scaling when the selected database provides appropriate capabilities.
limitations: Actual capacity depends on the database and its configuration.
Partitioning, replication, and consistency guarantees must be evaluated.
The design still needs a safe uniqueness strategy.
tradeoffs: Key-based access efficiency versus data-model and operational constraints.

followUpQuestions.prompt: Why does the system need a unique short code?
expectedAnswerPoints: Each code must resolve to one intended mapping.
Duplicate codes can redirect users to the wrong destination.
Uniqueness must hold under concurrent creation.
commonMisconceptions: Assuming a random generator guarantees uniqueness.

followUpQuestions.prompt: Why is an index on shortCode useful?
expectedAnswerPoints: Redirect requests search by short code.
An appropriate index can avoid scanning every mapping.
Indexes have storage and write-maintenance costs.

followUpQuestions.prompt: Why might a cache improve redirect performance?
expectedAnswerPoints: Repeated lookups can be served without reading the primary database.
Database read load may decrease.
Cache misses still require a lookup.
Cache behavior depends on access patterns and hit ratio.

followUpQuestions.prompt: How would you prevent two concurrent requests from creating conflicting short codes?
expectedAnswerPoints: Use an atomic uniqueness constraint or equivalent allocation mechanism.
Handle conflicts safely.
Retry or allocate a different identifier when appropriate.
Do not rely solely on a prior existence check.

followUpQuestions.prompt: What would you change if redirect traffic increased tenfold?
expectedAnswerPoints: Recalculate peak request rate.
Identify the limiting component.
Evaluate application scaling and database capacity.
Consider caching and uneven traffic distribution.
Avoid scaling components without evidence of a bottleneck.

followUpQuestions.prompt: What happens if the primary database becomes unavailable?
expectedAnswerPoints: New URL creation may need to fail or be deferred.
Cache hits may continue to work if the cache remains available and contains valid mappings.
Cache misses cannot be resolved from an unavailable database.
Replicas and failover may improve availability, depending on the design.
Consistency and recovery trade-offs must be considered.

followUpQuestions.prompt: Compare sequential IDs encoded with Base62, random short codes, and preallocated ID ranges.
expectedAnswerPoints: Sequential IDs can be simple but may expose creation patterns.
Random codes require collision handling.
Preallocated ranges can reduce central coordination but require safe allocation.
Identifier length, predictability, coordination, and collision probability matter.

followUpQuestions.prompt: How would you adapt the architecture for users distributed across several continents?
expectedAnswerPoints: Evaluate geographic latency.
Consider regional deployment and routing.
Choose an appropriate replication strategy.
Define consistency expectations.
Address regional failure and recovery.

sections.title: Analyze the workload
sections.content: Redirect traffic is ten times the URL creation traffic under the default assumptions. This makes lookup performance an important design consideration.

sections.title: Separate the request flows
sections.content: URL creation writes a mapping, while redirection resolves a mapping. Keeping these flows distinct makes their capacity and failure characteristics easier to reason about.

sections.title: Choose storage around access patterns
sections.content: The redirect path retrieves records by short code. A suitable key-based lookup and uniqueness mechanism are more important than choosing a database solely by its category.

sections.title: Add caching when justified
sections.content: A cache can reduce repeated database reads, particularly when access is concentrated on popular links. Its effectiveness depends on the hit ratio, workload distribution, and failure behavior.

sections.title: Handle uniqueness correctly
sections.content: Generating a candidate code is not enough. The system needs a concurrency-safe mechanism that prevents conflicting mappings.

sections.title: Evaluate failures
sections.content: Application redundancy does not eliminate database failure. Each dependency should have explicit failure behavior, and the architecture should not claim functionality it cannot provide.

commonMistakes.title: Treating the cache as the source of truth
commonMistakes.explanation: A cache may evict entries or become unavailable. Durable mapping storage is still required unless a different durable architecture is explicitly designed.

commonMistakes.title: Assuming random codes cannot collide
commonMistakes.explanation: Random generation does not guarantee uniqueness. The design must handle collisions safely.

commonMistakes.title: Adding components without a reason
commonMistakes.explanation: Every additional component introduces complexity. Components should be justified by a requirement, workload, or operational need.

commonMistakes.title: Claiming a latency guarantee from a diagram
commonMistakes.explanation: A diagram does not establish production latency. Estimates require workload inputs, component assumptions, and a clearly defined model.
